correctness.rationale: PASS: Explicit Gram/integral identities give F_q. A finite signed derivative measure reduces all real BV data to jumps, and jump discontinuity locations give rigidity. Strict monotonicity of a power secant slope selects the winning half. The second derivative is quadratic in s^q, giving exactly three stationary roots for q>1; for q<1 the transformed derivative is strictly concave on the favored half, with a unique zero. The q=1 polynomial reduction and envelope differentiation give the exact one-sided cusp slopes. The standalone checker ran 15770 finite identity/quadrature/grid checks, supplementary only.

value.rationale: PASS: The space span{1,x^q} is the simplest genuine Müntz deformation of classical linear least squares. Sharp integrated error for BV jumps is the natural worst-case approximation benchmark. The unique optimizer jumps discontinuously between macroscopically separated knots across the classical exponent, and the sharp squared error has computable distinct slopes. A global continuum parameter-classification with equality cases is more than an isolated tabulation or textbook norm estimate.
